object.definition: An object is a thing that you can touch, but it is not alive.
object.sentence: The object of soccer is to kick the ball into the other team's net.

objective.definition: An objective is something that you are trying to do.
objective.sentence: The main objective of our visit was to climb Mount Kenya.

obligation.definition: An obligation is a duty, something you must do.
obligation.sentence: Every right implies a responsibility; every opportunity, an obligation; every possession, a duty.

observation.definition: Observation is the act of carefully seeing things that happen.
observation.sentence: To learn, you must be good at observation.

observe.definition: If you observe something, you see or notice it.
observe.sentence: My goal is to record what I observe during one session.

obvious.definition: If something is obvious, it is easy to see it, think of it, or understand it.
obvious.sentence: It is obvious that you can't spend a lot of money and save at the same time.

obviously.definition: If something is obviously true, then it is very easy to see that it is true.
obviously.sentence: China is obviously much bigger than Japan.

occasion.definition: An occasion is a particular time.
occasion.sentence: The visit to Ottawa was a good occasion for us to get together.

occasionally.definition: If something happens occasionally, then it happens sometimes, but not often.
occasionally.sentence: I occasionally get nosebleeds when I fly.

occupy.definition: If something occupies a space, it is there, lives there, or belongs there.
occupy.sentence: Her personal apartment has two bedrooms. In New York this is sometimes more space than entire families occupy.

occur.sentence: Precious stones occur in a large area in Brazil.

ocean.definition: An ocean is a large area of salt water.
ocean.sentence: She stood on a beach in Japan and looked east at the sun coming up over the Pacific ocean.

odd.definition: If something is odd, it is not normal and usually you don't like it or don't understand it.
odd.sentence: The neighbours thought him very odd, because he would leave his doors open all night.

off.definition: Away from somewhere or some time.
off.sentence: There's a nice restaurant just off the main road.

offense.definition: An offense is an action that breaks the law.
offense.sentence: I didn't mean to give offense, but I didn't know that you don't do that in China.

offer.definition: An offer is when you say you will do something or give something.

office.definition: An office is a room or building where people sit at desks and work.
office.sentence: Her office is in the third door on the left side of the hall.

officer.definition: An officer is a person in an army who has much authority. A general and a captain are two types of officers.
officer.sentence: A soldier must obey his commanding officer.

official.definition: Something that is official is approved by some authority.
official.sentence: The letter was an official document from the president.

often.definition: When something happens often, that means that it happens many times and frequently.
often.sentence: I drink a lot of water and need to urinate often.

oil.definition: Oil is a liquid that is burned to create heat or used in machines to make them run well.
oil.sentence: Gas and oil are essential to running a car.

okay.definition: You use okay to show that you agree with something.

old.definition: If someone or something is old, they are not young; they have been in existence for a long time.
old.sentence: An old man has gray hair.

on.sentence: The circus traveled on to the next city.

one.sentence: One is the smallest whole number.

online.definition: On a regular route of a railroad or bus or airline system.

only.definition: No more than; no other than; just.
only.sentence: There are only three schools in this town.

open.definition: To move something to the side to allow entrance.
open.sentence: I will open the door for our guests.

opera.definition: An opera is a story told by actors singing instead of speaking, along with an orchestra.
opera.sentence: The couple dressed up to go hear their favorite opera at the theatre.

operate.definition: If you operate a machine, you control it.
operate.sentence: Everyone on board is able to operate the ship.

operation.definition: An operation is a medical process, often opening the human body.
operation.sentence: The doctors performed the operation in three hours.

operator.definition: An operator is a person who operates something.
operator.sentence: Jo is the operator of the tractor.

opinion.definition: An opinion is a personal idea, a person’s thoughts on a topic.
opinion.sentence: You gave your opinion of the case.

opponent.definition: An opponent is someone who is not in your team in a game, an opposite team.

opportunity.definition: An opportunity is a time, place, or situation in which something can happen, usually something good.
opportunity.sentence: Sleep provides an opportunity for the body to repair itself.

oppose.definition: If you oppose something, you try to stop it or fight against it.
oppose.sentence: We would strongly oppose any changes.

opposite.definition: If two things are opposite, they are the same kind but completely different from each other.
opposite.sentence: I don't think we can work together. We're too opposite.

opposition.definition: Opposition to something, is an action or hope to stop it.
opposition.sentence: There was strong opposition to the change from parents.

option.sentence: He has the option to go to university or join the army.

orange.definition: One of the colors people can see. It is lighter than red but darker than yellow.

order.definition: Order is when things are where they should be.
order.sentence: I need to take some time to put my things in order.

ordinary.definition: If something is ordinary, it is normal and not special.

organic.definition: If something is organic, it is related to or derived from living organisms.

organization.definition: An organization is a group of people with a particular purpose (e.g., teams, clubs, churches, etc.)
organization.sentence: The daycare is operated by a voluntary organization of parents and teachers.

organize.definition: When you organize something, you plan or arrange it.
organize.sentence: Can you help me organize my files?

origin.definition: The origin of something is its beginning.
origin.sentence: The origin of the universe can be explained with the Big Bang theory.

original.definition: The original person or thing, happened or existed before others of its kind.
original.sentence: The book has been translated from the original Russian version.

originally.definition: If something happens originally, it happens at the beginning of it.

other.definition: The other people or things, are those apart from the ones we have or were talking about.
other.sentence: No, don't put it on this table. Put it on the other table.

otherwise.definition: You use otherwise to connect two clauses where the second clause shows the bad thing that would happen if the first clause doesn't happen.
otherwise.sentence: You need the proper license. Otherwise you can't do business.

ought.definition: If you ought to do something, doing it is better than not doing it.
ought.sentence: I think perhaps we ought to help her.

out.definition: If you out somebody, you make public something they don't want others to know, especially that they are homosexual.

outcome.definition: An outcome is the result of a situation or action.
outcome.sentence: The outcome of the race was different from what most people were expecting.

outline.definition: An outline is a sketch that shows the general shape of an object.

output.definition: Output is what is produced by a worker, machine, computer, etc.
output.sentence: Of course, any problems with the program will affect the output.

outside.definition: Relating to or being on or near the outer side or limit.

over.definition: Something is over when it has finished, usually referring to an event.
over.sentence: When the movie was over we left the movie theater.

overall.definition: An overall effect, strategy, picture, etc., is one that covers everything but may not go into detail.
overall.sentence: The play has many Christian elements, but the overall effect is not necessarily Christian.

owe.definition: If you owe a person, there is something you need to pay or give to that person. That is, you owe something to that person.
owe.sentence: Thanks for the help! I really owe you for that!

own.definition: If something is your own it belongs to you or is about you (often used for emphasis).
own.sentence: I wish I had my own home.

owner.definition: The owner of a thing is the person who owns the thing: who has the thing or who should have the thing. A thing belongs to its owner.
owner.sentence: Who is the owner of this coat that was left on a chair?

ownership.definition: Ownership is the condition of being an owner.
